/article/detail/290.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN's Low-Carbon Intelligent Prefabricated Bus Stop Design won first prize in the 2024 Longgang Trade Union Cup employee innovation competition in Pingdi. Organized by the Longgang Federation of Trade Unions and hosted by Pingdi's trade union, the competition received 33 entries from ten enterprises.

The competition recognized small innovations, inventions, creations, designs and suggestions in equipment, technology, processes, management and service. Entries were assessed for originality, technical solutions, economic and social benefits and on-site presentations.

GSIN's design integrates prefabricated construction, intelligent public-transport systems, photovoltaic generation and wireless charging. It connects buses, rail and shared bicycles for the last kilometre of green travel, while offering charging, vending and first-aid services.

The International Low Carbon City station project in Pingdi, formerly the Tongxing Factory bus stop, illustrates connections with Metro Line 3 and the Shenzhen–Huizhou intercity railway, upgraded public facilities and low-carbon technology displays. GSIN will continue R&D and commercialization of urban-service buildings.

On 13 December, a four-person delegation from the Shenzhen Green Building Association, led by Secretary-General Wang Xiangyu, visited GSIN, an association vice-president member. Chairman Zhang Feng and representatives of the urban-service products division and general office received the visitors.

The exchange reviewed cooperation, business operations and opportunities for higher-quality green-building development. The association recognized GSIN's provincial demonstration projects, including Cumark Tower, Taizhou Nanyun Jiayuan and the Yuncheng Jinxiu Lijing project, and its prefabricated steel-structure light-panel system.

Zhang introduced GSIN's prefabricated steel villas, combining low-carbon design, circular-economy principles and Eastern aesthetics to provide safe, functional and affordable homes. He proposed a show home integrating steel prefabrication, photovoltaic technology and low-carbon industrial-chain resources. The association welcomed further discussion of cooperation among its members.

The group toured light-gauge and heavy-steel villa show homes and discussed comfort and construction quality. Both sides looked forward to further exchanges supporting Shenzhen's green-building industry.

/article/detail/288.html.title: Steel structure topped out at Xichong Depot, Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III
/article/detail/288.html.summary: On the afternoon of 10 December, the final large-section steel beam, weighing 11 tonnes, was installed at Xichong Depot on Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III, marking completion of the steel structure delivered by GSIN.
/article/detail/288.html.bodyHtml:
On the afternoon of 10 December, the final large-section steel beam, weighing 11 tonnes, was installed at Xichong Depot on Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III, marking completion of the steel structure delivered by GSIN.

The depot lies in Xichong Community, Kuichong Subdistrict, Dapeng New District, north of the Yanba Expressway and west of a planned green corridor. Maintenance and operating sheds have a staggered layout. The project reserves conditions for over-depot development, including a platform of approximately 100,000 m² and 15 buildings within and around it.

GSIN's work covers the maintenance shed and throat areas 2, 3 and 4, with approximately 5,000 tonnes of steel. The maintenance shed uses a fully braced frame and sloping roof at 14.000 m, equivalent to an absolute elevation of 20.600 m. Its encased steelwork uses welded built-up sections, with 15 columns and 32 beams installed at approximately 14 m.

Maintenance-shed beam sections include welded H2000×700×38×48, H1700×500×30×42 and H1100–500×500×30×42. The lifting campaign involved 166 beams weighing approximately 366 tonnes, mainly Q335B steel as recorded in the original article.

The throat areas use steel-reinforced concrete frames. Area 3 has two floor slabs, 27 columns weighing approximately 370 tonnes and 50 beams weighing approximately 480 tonnes, with maximum fabricated length of 27 m in Q355B. Areas 2 and 4 have five column types and respectively 42 and 38 columns, primarily Q355B.

Heavy columns exceeded 30 tonnes each, with 15 columns fabricated full-length. Individual beams weighed up to 24 tonnes and typical spans reached 32.400 m. The team used rational segmentation and large lifting equipment; seven oversized throat-area beams were assembled on site before lifting. GSIN emphasized safe delivery through coordinated construction and quality control.

Following the April launch of GSIN Homes' nationwide show-home programme, a client from Meizhou, Guangdong, visited the company several times for inspection and discussions. After evaluation, GSIN agreed to build the Qiu family villa as a prefabricated steel-structure show home.

The agreement was signed on 5 November and construction started on 17 November, with a planned programme of three to four months. Having worked in Shenzhen for more than 30 years, the client intended to return to Meizhou after retirement to live closer to his parents.

The client selected a modern Chinese style. GSIN's design team conducted site visits and refined the design to suit the family's needs and local architectural character. GSIN Homes offers Chinese, European and modern villa styles.

At the time of this historical announcement, selected projects under the nationwide show-home programme could receive a construction discount of RMB 500 per square metre. The original promotional graphic and historical contact information are retained below.

/article/detail/283.html.title: Steel construction completed at Wuchuan's smart multi-storey parking garage
/article/detail/283.html.summary: GSIN completed steel construction for two smart mechanical parking garages in Wuchuan, Guangdong. Removal of their external scaffolding marked completion of the steelwork. The facilities address parking demand in a densely developed urban area.
/article/detail/283.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN completed steel construction for two smart mechanical parking garages in Wuchuan, Guangdong. Removal of their external scaffolding marked completion of the steelwork. The facilities address parking demand in a densely developed urban area.

The municipal smart-parking programme includes three garages at the former forestry bureau dormitory on Gongye First Road, the Shanjiaoqiao vacant plot at Xinjian Road and Tangchang Road, and the fisheries company office on Keping Road. The developer is the Wuchuan Urban Management and Comprehensive Law Enforcement Bureau.

GSIN delivered steelwork at Shanjiaoqiao and the former forestry bureau site, using approximately 857 tonnes of steel in total. Both use vertical-lift mechanical parking systems, reinforced-concrete basements and steel-framed above-ground structures.

The Shanjiaoqiao garage is a prefabricated steel building with one basement and nine above-ground levels, a floor area of 3,836.41 m², standard storey heights of 2.5 m/2.0 m, a building height of 23.95 m and a plan of 19.35 m × 21.20 m.

At Shanjiaoqiao, 30 equipment foundation plates are embedded at −2.300 m and 44 at −0.800 m. The steel-frame base elevation is −0.250 m; storey heights include 3.68, 2.50, 2.00, 2.25 and 2.12 m. Roof structure and plant-room roof elevations are 21.550 m and 23.670 m. Twenty box columns are arranged on five transverse and four longitudinal axes; hot-rolled H beams use Q355B.

Level 2 uses HB1-90 steel-truss floor decking with a 120 mm total floor thickness and rail embeds. Levels 3–9 include maintenance walkways and oil-drip protection, using No. 12 channels, angles, mesh and 0.6 mm profiled steel sheet. The south and north roof sides and plant-room roof use HB1-90 decking and 6 mm patterned steel plate. Original drawings and the former forestry bureau garage specifications are retained in the illustrated report below.

/article/detail/280.html.title: Construction begins on Hongji Xiyue Tower
/article/detail/280.html.summary: Steel construction began at Hongji Xiyue Tower with the successful lifting of a 2.9-tonne column. GSIN is responsible for steelwork on Tower 1.
/article/detail/280.html.bodyHtml:
Steel construction began at Hongji Xiyue Tower with the successful lifting of a 2.9-tonne column. GSIN is responsible for steelwork on Tower 1.

Located at Longgang Avenue and Xipu West Street in Shenzhen, the commercial and office building is 119.15 m high, with three basement levels and 30 above-ground storeys, using a frame-core structural system. Floor area is 64,616.89 m². The developer is Tunghsu Azure Renewable Energy Co., Ltd.; the general contractor is Shenzhen Wancheng Construction Engineering Co., Ltd.

Approximately 855 tonnes of steel are used in encased circular outer-frame columns, podium H-section columns, steel-reinforced concrete H beams and roof framing. Seventeen tower steel columns extend from basement level 3 to level 21; levels 19–21 include 14 inclined circular columns. Two podium H-section columns extend from levels 2–4, while 17 box columns run from level 24 to the roof framing.

Encased beams occur between basement level 2 and level 21, concentrated on levels 19–21. Roof beams are box sections. Steel grade is Q355B, with a maximum plate thickness of 50 mm. GSIN will coordinate closely with the client, general contractor and supervisor.

/article/detail/281.html.title: Warehouse No. 1 steel structure topped out at the Guangzhou Yihai Kerry project
/article/detail/281.html.summary: Warehouse 1 at Yihai Kerry's South China grain and oil production, sales and integrated food-processing base in Guangzhou topped out its main steel structure. GSIN is responsible for the project's steel construction.
/article/detail/281.html.bodyHtml:
Warehouse 1 at Yihai Kerry's South China grain and oil production, sales and integrated food-processing base in Guangzhou topped out its main steel structure. GSIN is responsible for the project's steel construction.

The project occupies 156,919.00 m² on plot XJ-5-1 north of Xiji Road, Xiagang Subdistrict, Huangpu District, Guangzhou, with a floor area of 416,495.83 m². It includes warehouses and workshops with steel and concrete frames. The developer is Yihai Kerry (Guangzhou) Food Industries Co., Ltd.; the general contractor is China Construction First Group.

Steelwork is concentrated in Warehouse 1 and wall purlins on other buildings. Warehouse 1 uses circular columns, welded H beams, buckling-restrained braces, wall purlins and steel stairs in Q355B. The largest circular column is D950×30; maximum primary and secondary beam sections are BH900–1150×600×20×36 and BH900×400×10×18. Floor decking includes TD4-90, TD4-120 and TD4-170 steel-truss systems.

Warehouse walls use C-section purlins and rock-wool sandwich panels. Buildings 2, 4, 5 and 8 use embeds, square tubes, C purlins and rock-wool panels. Total project steel is estimated at 9,600 tonnes; the heaviest beam component is about 6.5 tonnes.

Warehouse 1 is 89.7 m long and 86.5 m wide, with one basement, seven above-ground storeys and a height of 57 m. Its approximately 8,600 tonnes of steel account for about 90% of the project total. The team will complete remaining wall purlins and steelwork to the client and general contractor's requirements.

/article/detail/279.html.title: Guangzhou New China Life Insurance Tower wins the Yuegang Award
/article/detail/279.html.summary: Guangzhou New China Life Insurance Tower received the 16th Guangdong Steel Structure Gold Award, or Yuegang Award, in the construction category. The original report records September 2024. Organized by the Guangdong Steel Structure Association, the award recognizes high-quality steel construction in the province.
/article/detail/279.html.bodyHtml:
Guangzhou New China Life Insurance Tower received the 16th Guangdong Steel Structure Gold Award, or Yuegang Award, in the construction category. The original report records September 2024. Organized by the Guangdong Steel Structure Association, the award recognizes high-quality steel construction in the province.

The Grade A office tower is 180 m high, with 41 above-ground storeys including a six-storey podium and four basement levels. It occupies 8,423 m², with a total floor area of 133,825.8 m²: 105,319.9 m² above ground and 28,505.9 m² below. The main structure combines a concrete core with an outer steel frame.

Its 47.4 m × 47.4 m steel frame includes 16 outer box columns tapering upwards and three H columns inside the core. Steel floor beams on levels 6–42 connect the core to the columns. Q355B steelwork totals approximately 8,500 tonnes, with around 60,000 m² of decking and 76,000 m² of fire-protection coating.

Limited laydown space and crane coverage required tightly controlled delivery sequences, optimized site layout and access routes. Thick-plate welding, including 45 mm column plates, required wind protection, controlled interpass temperatures, preheating and postheating, deformation control, experienced welders, symmetric CO₂-shielded welding and ultrasonic testing.

The team coordinated erection sequences with civil engineers, used temporary guy-wire restraints and monitored column displacement to maintain installation accuracy. GSIN welcomed the award as recognition of project quality and its steel-construction capabilities.

/article/detail/277.html.title: Construction begins on Hainan Art Museum
/article/detail/277.html.summary: On the morning of 21 July, steel construction began at Hainan Provincial Art Museum. An 85-tonne-capacity mobile crane lifted steel beam NC-GKL1-29, weighing 4.4 tonnes. GSIN is responsible for the steelwork.
/article/detail/277.html.bodyHtml:
On the morning of 21 July, steel construction began at Hainan Provincial Art Museum. An 85-tonne-capacity mobile crane lifted steel beam NC-GKL1-29, weighing 4.4 tonnes. GSIN is responsible for the steelwork.

The museum occupies plots JDWH-04-A03/A04 in Haikou's Jiangdong New Area international cultural district, south of Wenming East Tunnel and facing the Nandu River. It has one basement and four above-ground storeys on a 67,348 m² site, with a floor area of 33,600 m².

The structure uses reinforced-concrete shear walls with steel roof beams and composite steel-truss decking. The developer is Haikou's tourism, culture, radio, television and sports authority; the general contractor is China Construction First Group.

Steelwork from level 1 to the roof includes encased columns, steel columns, beams and embeds. Columns include H, cruciform and square-tube sections; beams are H and square-tube sections, mainly Q390GJC. Embeds connect steel columns and beams to the concrete structure. Total steel is estimated at 3,600 tonnes.

The completed museum will provide multifunctional public cultural facilities. GSIN committed to quality, efficiency and timely delivery.

/article/detail/270.html.title: The Song of GSIN: Celebrating 26 years of development
/article/detail/270.html.summary: Some say that choosing construction means choosing poetry and distant horizons. In the sands of Urumqi, beside the ports of Beibu Gulf, at the docks of Xiamen Island and on the fertile Jianghan Plain, we pursue the dream of green buildings, wherever the road may lead. Wherever the construction site stands, there is our home.
/article/detail/270.html.bodyHtml:
Some say that choosing construction means choosing poetry and distant horizons. In the sands of Urumqi, beside the ports of Beibu Gulf, at the docks of Xiamen Island and on the fertile Jianghan Plain, we pursue the dream of green buildings, wherever the road may lead. Wherever the construction site stands, there is our home.

Beneath swirling snow, steel pipe supports dance in the air. Wind and horns intertwine; snowflakes mingle with welding sparks, playing a heroic symphony. Its leading performers are those eagles of the snowy land, the steel backbone beneath the Tianshan Mountains.

The scorching sun blazes and torrential rain pours. Work continues through day and night; lights illuminate the empty site as every minute counts. Bricks become pillows and steel plates become beds, sustained by an iron resolve to finish on schedule and a steel determination to deliver. Three hundred and ninety-six artists make the march of steel ring out across Guangming Science City.

The detailer uses professional knowledge to tailor prefabricated buildings. The materials specialist watches every steel plate with a discerning eye. The welder's dedication ignites the sparks that join steel. The construction engineer measures every inch of the steel skybridge with steady steps. The quality inspector examines every component with responsibility and sound judgement. The safety officer, meticulous and focused, shoulders the priceless responsibility of protecting lives.

Their hardworking hands bring colour to buildings. Their intelligence nurtures the prosperity of cities. Their physical and mental effort creates history cast in place, silent music, motionless dance and enduring art.

Through twenty-six years of hard beginnings and perseverance, through heat and cold and difficult challenges, landmarks have risen across the country: Jinxi Meishu Mansion, Taizhou Nanyun Jiayuan, Huiyun Center above the metro, Shenzhen Bay One, the international exhibition center welcoming visitors from around the world, Guangzhou's thermal power plant lighting thousands of homes, and Shenzhen Stock Exchange, a stage for finance and capital.

Louder than the wind is the roar of machinery. Quieter than the rain is the promise within. Firmer than the frost is the conviction of steel-structure builders. We renew and improve, strengthen ourselves, cultivate green construction and work towards a zero-carbon future. Having chosen a distant destination, we press on through wind and rain: building with life.

Afterword: Since its founding in 1998, GSIN has travelled through twenty-six years of challenges and progress. This poem honours every GSIN colleague who has devoted themselves to steel-structure construction during those years.

Acknowledgements: Some lines quote or adapt Wang Guozhen's Love of Life, Li Chunyun's Construction Workers Have Strength, and A Poem for Construction Workers by Shaanxi Construction Hangcheng Company. 25 June 2024.

/article/detail/273.html.title: GSIN passes the 2024 Shenzhen Prefabricated Building Industrial Base assessment
/article/detail/273.html.summary: GSIN passed the 2024 Shenzhen prefabricated-building industrial-base assessment organized by the municipal housing authority. Chairman Zhang Feng, senior managers and departmental representatives received the expert panel.
/article/detail/273.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN passed the 2024 Shenzhen prefabricated-building industrial-base assessment organized by the municipal housing authority. Chairman Zhang Feng, senior managers and departmental representatives received the expert panel.

The panel heard presentations, inspected the fabrication workshops, reviewed production processes and methods and examined evidence covering engineering delivery, technical innovation and talent development. It scored the company against the assessment criteria and discussed current operations.

Experts recognized GSIN's professionalism and achievements and encouraged further innovation and training to support high-quality development across Shenzhen's prefabricated-building supply chain.

The industrial-base programme recognizes organizations with clear objectives, mature technology, strong R&D and training, and the scale and capability to lead the industry. GSIN received Guangdong and Shenzhen component-production base recognition in 2019 and national prefabricated-building industrial-base recognition in 2020.

/article/detail/274.html.title: Pingdi's Safety Home inaugurated at GSIN
/article/detail/274.html.summary: On 4 July, Pingdi's Safety Home pilot was inaugurated at GSIN. Representatives of emergency management, trade unions, fire rescue and market supervision attended, together with more than 30 local enterprises.
/article/detail/274.html.bodyHtml:
On 4 July, Pingdi's Safety Home pilot was inaugurated at GSIN. Representatives of emergency management, trade unions, fire rescue and market supervision attended, together with more than 30 local enterprises.

Pingdi Party committee secretary Ye Junhui called for a demonstration center connecting government and businesses through safety education, knowledge sharing, skills development, hazard analysis and emergency drills.

Shenzhen Jinxin Steel Structure Co., Ltd., a wholly owned GSIN subsidiary, was designated a Safety Home pilot organization. GSIN committed to safety training, management exchanges and wider participation by local businesses.

Emergency-management experts provided training, including safety videos and an explanation of the latest Work Safety Law. GSIN will establish the organization, clarify responsibilities and implement activities under the platform's operating rules.

/article/detail/275.html.title: GSIN holds a series of Work Safety Month activities
/article/detail/275.html.summary: In June 2024, GSIN organized Work Safety Month activities under the theme of safety awareness, emergency readiness and clear escape routes, following national guidance and the principle of prevention and comprehensive safety management.
/article/detail/275.html.bodyHtml:
In June 2024, GSIN organized Work Safety Month activities under the theme of safety awareness, emergency readiness and clear escape routes, following national guidance and the principle of prevention and comprehensive safety management.

A company-wide launch meeting took place on 30 May through headquarters and project-site video links, organized by the safety and delivery management department and chaired by the executive deputy general manager. The fabrication plant held its launch that afternoon, with projects organizing local sessions. Safety videos, accident case studies and information displays reinforced awareness.

Project and factory managers led hazard inspections. The executive deputy general manager also led second-quarter inspections in early and mid-June, emphasizing safety, rectification notices, deadlines and accountability.

Headquarters and factory personnel practiced fire response, electric-shock rescue and lifting/object-strike accident response. Training included extinguisher use, firefighting equipment, rescue precautions and CPR. Safety quizzes and summer refreshments accompanied the activities; projects also ran their own drills.

The programme strengthened emergency response, evacuation skills and staff participation. GSIN will continue improving safety systems and maintaining orderly production.

/article/detail/269.html.title: GSIN conducts comprehensive project inspections for the second quarter of 2024
/article/detail/269.html.summary: In early and mid-June, GSIN inspected eight key active projects in Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Zhanjiang and other locations as part of its second-quarter 2024 comprehensive review.
/article/detail/269.html.bodyHtml:
In early and mid-June, GSIN inspected eight key active projects in Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Zhanjiang and other locations as part of its second-quarter 2024 comprehensive review.

Led by the executive deputy general manager and organized by the safety and delivery management department, the team included finance, technical management, supply chain, audit and general-office managers. Reviews covered safety, finance, technology, production, commercial management, materials, administration and quality.

The team heard project reports, inspected sites, reviewed records and scored each item against a standard assessment sheet. Follow-up meetings examined strengths, problems, solutions and feedback from frontline staff.

Written findings were issued to each project. Rewards or penalties followed the company's management red-line rules; rectification notices set deadlines and required reinspection. The programme aimed to strengthen project-delivery responsibilities and maintain efficient, stable construction.

/article/detail/267.html.title: First large-section steel beam lifted at Xichong Depot, Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III
/article/detail/267.html.summary: On 7 June, a 26.5-tonne large-section steel beam was successfully lifted into position at Xichong Depot on Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III. GSIN's team completed the first lift despite persistent rain, following the planned lifting and safety procedures.
/article/detail/267.html.bodyHtml:
On 7 June, a 26.5-tonne large-section steel beam was successfully lifted into position at Xichong Depot on Shenzhen Metro Line 8 Phase III. GSIN's team completed the first lift despite persistent rain, following the planned lifting and safety procedures.

The depot lies in a trapezoidal area north of the Yanba Expressway and west of a planned green corridor, with staggered maintenance and operating sheds. Future over-depot development includes a platform of approximately 100,000 m² and 15 buildings within and around it.

GSIN's maintenance-shed and throat-area work uses approximately 5,000 tonnes of steel. The maintenance shed's encased steelwork comprises welded built-up sections, with 15 columns and 32 beams at approximately 14 m elevation. Beam sections are welded H2000×700×38×48, H1700×500×30×42 and H1100–500×500×30×42.

The milestone established a sound start to construction. GSIN will continue to coordinate safety, quality and progress for timely delivery and the future opening of Metro Line 8 Phase III.

/article/detail/263.html.title: International cargo warehouse tops out at Guangzhou Baiyun Airport Phase III's east cargo area
/article/detail/263.html.summary: On 3 June, the international cargo warehouse at the Phase III east cargo area of Guangzhou Baiyun Airport was successfully topped out. GSIN is responsible for steel construction on the project.
/article/detail/263.html.bodyHtml:
On 3 June, the international cargo warehouse at the Phase III east cargo area of Guangzhou Baiyun Airport was successfully topped out. GSIN is responsible for steel construction on the project.

Project overview: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Phase III Expansion Cargo Area Works. The site lies at the airside–landside boundary between the second and third eastern runways, north of Terminal T3 and the reserved future satellite terminal. It occupies 84,913.38 m², with a floor area of 110,528 m² and estimated steel consumption of approximately 5,800 tonnes.

Both the international and domestic cargo terminals use portal-frame steel structures with a maximum span of 72 m. The international terminal is 272 m long and 11.5 m high, using 1,695.8 tonnes of steel. Its steel beams are assembled and spliced on site before being lifted in three sections.

The photographs show the project team's site managers, the relative positions of the cargo areas, the international terminal's steel structure and construction activities. A rare double rainbow appeared over the site shortly before topping out.

Completion of the international warehouse marks a strong start. GSIN will continue with the larger domestic warehouse, working towards high-quality contract delivery.

/article/detail/259.html.title: Shenzhen SEZ Construction Science and Industry Group delegation visits GSIN
/article/detail/259.html.summary: On 16 May, a delegation from Shenzhen SEZ Construction Science and Industry Group Co., Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Shenzhen SEZ Construction Group, visited GSIN, a National Prefabricated Building Industrial Base. The delegation included Deputy General Manager Peng Lingchuan, Finance Director Li Hui and Wu Fang of the business management center. GSIN Chairman Zhang Feng and senior managers, together with the heads of steel fabrication, financial management, audit and the general office, welcomed the visitors.
/article/detail/259.html.bodyHtml:
On 16 May, a delegation from Shenzhen SEZ Construction Science and Industry Group Co., Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Shenzhen SEZ Construction Group, visited GSIN, a National Prefabricated Building Industrial Base. The delegation included Deputy General Manager Peng Lingchuan, Finance Director Li Hui and Wu Fang of the business management center. GSIN Chairman Zhang Feng and senior managers, together with the heads of steel fabrication, financial management, audit and the general office, welcomed the visitors.

Peng Lingchuan and Zhang Feng introduced their companies' business scope, operating scale and organization. Discussions covered how factories undertake work, management and labour allocation, downstream pricing and settlement, contracting arrangements, management remuneration and manufacturing cost control.

The delegation praised GSIN's expertise in green construction and expressed interest in further exchanges and cooperation. GSIN is a national high-tech enterprise working in super high-rise, large-span and prefabricated steel structures, with Grade I specialist steel-structure contracting qualification. The company welcomes visitors interested in green construction to discuss potential cooperation.

/article/detail/260.html.title: GSIN wins the Hainan Art Museum contract
/article/detail/260.html.summary: GSIN has signed an engineering subcontract with the Hainan branch of China Construction First Group for Hainan Art Museum. GSIN is responsible for fabrication and erection of all steel structures, with work planned to begin in early June.
/article/detail/260.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN has signed an engineering subcontract with the Hainan branch of China Construction First Group for Hainan Art Museum. GSIN is responsible for fabrication and erection of all steel structures, with work planned to begin in early June.

Hainan Art Museum is one of the province's ten key public cultural infrastructure projects. Haikou's tourism, culture, radio, television and sports authority planned an investment of RMB 500 million and a total floor area of approximately 33,600 m². The museum will fill the gap in large provincial art museums in Hainan, supporting the exhibition, collection and research of important artworks and serving as a window for Hainan Free Trade Port culture.

GSIN's previous landmark projects in Hainan include the large-span steel structure of Danzhou Sports Center and the super high-rise Hainan Haikong Tower. The team will once again cross the Qiongzhou Strait to deliver a new landmark with its partners.

/article/detail/261.html.title: First roof truss lifted at Zhengzhou High-tech Urban Cultural Complex
/article/detail/261.html.summary: The first roof truss lift in Area 1 of Zhengzhou High-tech Urban Cultural Complex has been completed successfully. GSIN is responsible for the project's steel construction.
/article/detail/261.html.bodyHtml:
The first roof truss lift in Area 1 of Zhengzhou High-tech Urban Cultural Complex has been completed successfully. GSIN is responsible for the project's steel construction.

The public-building project occupies approximately 69,966.7 m² within the area bounded by Kexue Avenue, Chuangxin Avenue, Duying Street and Huanglan Road in Zhongyuan District, Zhengzhou. It has three above-ground storeys and one basement level, with estimated steel consumption of approximately 9,400 tonnes. The floor-area figure in the original release is written as 156000 ten-thousand m²; this historical source figure has not been independently corrected.

Construction is organized into four areas. Steel construction is concentrated in Area 1, with an estimated 7,400 tonnes, approximately 79% of the total. The lower main structure is a steel frame; the roof comprises inverted triangular tubular trusses connected to the steel frame columns through manufactured bearings.

The first roof truss lift marks entry into a critical stage. GSIN will continue to apply demanding standards to deliver the project with the required quality, quantity and schedule.

/article/detail/258.html.title: Notice: GSIN's participation in a 2023 Guangdong Science and Technology Award application

/article/detail/258.html.bodyHtml:
