/article/detail/252.html.title: Dongtai Ningxi Yuefu steel-structure housing named a Jiangsu new-building-industrialization demonstration project
/article/detail/252.html.summary: GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure housing at Ningxi Yuefu in Dongtai, Yancheng, received support under Jiangsu's 2022 Green Building Development Special Fund as a Green Building Quality Improvement Project, in the category of integrated new-building-industrialization technology demonstration.
/article/detail/252.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure housing at Ningxi Yuefu in Dongtai, Yancheng, received support under Jiangsu's 2022 Green Building Development Special Fund as a Green Building Quality Improvement Project, in the category of integrated new-building-industrialization technology demonstration.

The project has 25 above-ground storeys and two basement levels, a floor area of 10,971 m² and a height of 83.25 m, as stated in this news release. It addresses technical barriers to steel structures in high-rise housing and was featured in CCTV Finance's Steel Backbone documentary.

Its steel frame and bracing system uses square hollow-section columns. In June 2020, an expert panel led by Professor Shu Ganping of Southeast University reviewed the system and endorsed its suitability for high-rise steel housing.

The building uses GSIN's proprietary prefabricated steel-structure light-panel technology. H-section beams have unequal flange widths, with lower flanges narrower than the walls to avoid exposed beams. Some floors use removable steel-bar truss decking, allowing unfinished interiors to be handed over directly and the bottom formwork to be reused.

Interior walls use single ALC panels; exterior walls use an ALC panel–cavity–ALC panel enclosure. Suspended-platform installation and dry construction eliminate plastering, save water and materials, and integrate enclosure, insulation, fire resistance and waterproofing. The double-layer structure also improves energy performance.

Jiangsu's special fund supports greener urban and rural construction under carbon-peaking goals. GSIN's approach emphasizes quality, low energy consumption and building industrialization, demonstrating green design, technology, performance and operations to support high-quality industry development.

/article/detail/253.html.title: GSIN contributes to the newly released T/CECS 1051-2022 standard
/article/detail/253.html.summary: Technical Specification for Application of Autoclaved Lightweight Concrete Wall Panels (T/CECS 1051-2022) has been officially published. It was jointly led by Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, and GSIN, with contributions from Chongqing University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, China Institute of Building Standard Design & Research and other organizations.
/article/detail/253.html.bodyHtml:
Technical Specification for Application of Autoclaved Lightweight Concrete Wall Panels (T/CECS 1051-2022) has been officially published. It was jointly led by Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, and GSIN, with contributions from Chongqing University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, China Institute of Building Standard Design & Research and other organizations.

Prepared under the China Association for Engineering Construction Standardization's first 2019 standards development and revision plan (Jian Biao Xie Zi [2019] No. 12), the specification took effect on 1 August 2022. It covers materials, design, transport, installation and acceptance of autoclaved lightweight concrete wall panels, providing guidance for prefabricated steel-building envelopes and greener, more energy-efficient, low-carbon construction.

/article/detail/254.html.title: Wuxi's first prefabricated steel apartment project tops out
/article/detail/254.html.summary: On 15 December, the main structure of Building 8 at Wuxi CEC Innovation Park was topped out. Delivered by GSIN, it is Wuxi's first prefabricated steel-structure apartment project.
/article/detail/254.html.bodyHtml:
On 15 December, the main structure of Building 8 at Wuxi CEC Innovation Park was topped out. Delivered by GSIN, it is Wuxi's first prefabricated steel-structure apartment project.

Located in Xinwu District, Wuxi, the building has one basement level and 21 above-ground storeys, a total height of 70.2 m and a floor area of 14,041.39 m².

The high-rise apartment building uses GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure light-panel technology. Its main structure combines a steel frame with steel-plate shear walls. Exterior walls are double-layer composites of autoclaved aerated concrete panels and fibre-cement panels, installed externally on steel framing.

The project is delivered with finished interiors and has a prefabrication rate of 80.1%. It demonstrates open spaces, flexible layouts, seismic performance, rapid construction, quality and recyclability. The approach aims to reduce construction pollution and resource use while enabling low lifecycle energy consumption, replaceable components and maintainable buildings.

/article/detail/242.html.title: GSIN wins first prize in the 2022 Guangdong Steel Structure Science and Technology Awards
/article/detail/242.html.summary: GSIN's Research and Engineering Application of Complete Technologies for the GSIN Prefabricated Steel Structural System received first prize in the 2022 Guangdong Steel Structure Science and Technology Awards, presented by the Guangdong Steel Structure Association.
/article/detail/242.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN's Research and Engineering Application of Complete Technologies for the GSIN Prefabricated Steel Structural System received first prize in the 2022 Guangdong Steel Structure Science and Technology Awards, presented by the Guangdong Steel Structure Association.

GSIN led the work with Tsinghua University, the Shenzhen branch of China Academy of Building Research, China Wuzhou Engineering Group, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research, Hunan University of Science and Technology, Chongqing University and Shenzhen Youshe Housing Technology.

On 15 December 2021, a panel organized by the China Steel Construction Society and chaired by Academician Yue Qingrui evaluated the achievement. The panel rated the overall work internationally advanced, with the through-plate beam–column connection for prefabricated steel frames and the connection between new prefabricated reinforced-concrete floor slabs and steel beams reaching an internationally leading level.

/article/detail/231.html.title: GSIN mobile COVID-19 testing stations support Shenzhen's epidemic response
/article/detail/231.html.summary: GSIN's mobile COVID-19 sampling station has entered service at a testing site in Shatou Subdistrict, Futian. Medical workers sit inside the 3.6 m² station and take samples through openings in the glass enclosure, allowing separated sampling operations.
/article/detail/231.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN's mobile COVID-19 sampling station has entered service at a testing site in Shatou Subdistrict, Futian. Medical workers sit inside the 3.6 m² station and take samples through openings in the glass enclosure, allowing separated sampling operations.

Recurring outbreaks and routine testing created a need for safer, more comfortable working conditions. Hot southern summers and cold northern winters both challenge outdoor medical work. The station was designed to improve the sampling environment and protect frontline staff.

Ergonomic design: Many sampling stations require staff to stand for two or three hours. GSIN's inclined sampling window allows flexible seated operation for different users, reducing fatigue during extended sampling sessions.

Separation and protection: The workbench allows sampling, swab sealing and alcohol disinfection to be performed outside before tube boxes are collected inside in batches. Swabs carrying saliva do not enter the cabin directly. A positive-pressure fresh-air system further limits the entry of outside air.

Flexible deployment: Castors allow the station to move between locations. Following disinfection, it can also be lifted by crane and transported for reuse, supporting changing multi-site testing needs.

The station incorporates medical antibacterial wall panels, positive-pressure ventilation, ultraviolet disinfection, intelligent voice functions and an outdoor display to support safe, efficient sampling.

/article/detail/238.html.title: Shenzhen's first high-rise, long-span steel cold-storage roof successfully lifted
/article/detail/238.html.summary: On 8 July, GSIN successfully completed the overall lifting of the roof steel structure at Liguang Logistics Park. Located in Guanlan Subdistrict, Longhua District, Shenzhen, the park occupies approximately 45,300 m², with a total floor area of approximately 265,000 m². Shenzhen Jian'an Group is the general contractor and GSIN the specialist steel-structure contractor.
/article/detail/238.html.bodyHtml:
On 8 July, GSIN successfully completed the overall lifting of the roof steel structure at Liguang Logistics Park. Located in Guanlan Subdistrict, Longhua District, Shenzhen, the park occupies approximately 45,300 m², with a total floor area of approximately 265,000 m². Shenzhen Jian'an Group is the general contractor and GSIN the specialist steel-structure contractor.

This was Shenzhen's first overall lift of a high-rise, large-span steel cold-storage roof system. The roof space frame spans 42.7 m and was raised 48 m. After ground-level assembly and acceptance, hydraulic synchronized lifting at eight groups of lifting points completed the operation in six hours.

Factory fabrication reduced on-site welding and pollution. Ground-level assembly and overall lifting improved efficiency, shortened the programme and reduced the risks associated with conventional work at height.

The team's work supported quality delivery and the company's reputation. In the first half of 2022, Liguang Logistics Park received recognition as a Guangdong Municipal Engineering Work Safety and Civilized Construction Demonstration Site and a Shenzhen Excellent Construction Safety and Civilized Construction Site. The project is intended as an ecological, intelligent and innovative logistics complex providing one-stop urban logistics services.

/article/detail/239.html.title: Fangchenggang's first prefabricated steel residential structure tops out
/article/detail/239.html.summary: With the final steel beam installed, Building 5 at Jinxi Meishu Mansion, Fangchenggang's first prefabricated steel-structure residential project, was successfully topped out.
/article/detail/239.html.bodyHtml:
With the final steel beam installed, Building 5 at Jinxi Meishu Mansion, Fangchenggang's first prefabricated steel-structure residential project, was successfully topped out.

Located near Jinhuacha Avenue in Fangcheng District, Guangxi, the general-contracting project uses GSIN's prefabricated steel-building system. The structure combines a braced steel frame, precast concrete stairs and steel-bar truss floor decking. Its envelope combines light-gauge steel framing, externally mounted high-density fibre-cement panels and inset ALC panels. This finished, modern Chinese-style residential building has a total floor area of 7,171.48 m², a height of 54.6 m, 18 above-ground storeys and one basement level.

Green housing seeks to save energy, land, water and materials throughout its lifecycle, protect the environment, reduce pollution and provide healthy, comfortable, efficient spaces. Steel's machinability, ease of assembly and high strength-to-weight ratio suit modular, standardized, factory-made construction, reducing complex manual and wet work on site.

GSIN's light-panel steel-building system integrates the main steel structure, envelope, interiors, services and pipework. Its intended benefits include adaptable applications and layouts, rapid construction, reduced environmental impact, controlled costs, reliable performance and recyclability.

On 6 January 2021, Guangxi's housing authority designated Fangchenggang a regional pilot city for prefabricated steel housing (Gui Jian Han [2021] No. 9). As the city's first such housing project, Building 5 followed GSIN's complete construction process and strict quality controls to become a demonstration project.

GSIN has also undertaken Nanyun Jiayuan in Taizhou and Ningxi Yuefu in Dongtai, Jiangsu. The company will continue to use its light-panel steel-building system to support transformation, quality housing and the development of the prefabricated steel residential industry.

/article/detail/240.html.title: GSIN's Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development research project passes acceptance review
/article/detail/240.html.summary: GSIN has received a Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development Science and Technology Programme Project Acceptance Certificate. This confirms acceptance of the green-building and energy-efficiency demonstration project Application Technology for Prefabricated Steel-Structure Light-Panel Buildings at Cumark Tower.
/article/detail/240.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN has received a Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development Science and Technology Programme Project Acceptance Certificate. This confirms acceptance of the green-building and energy-efficiency demonstration project Application Technology for Prefabricated Steel-Structure Light-Panel Buildings at Cumark Tower.

Cumark Tower integrated and innovated its structural, envelope and interior systems. The project completed one municipal construction method, obtained one invention patent and 14 utility-model patents, prepared 11 system standards, published five research reports or papers and hosted more than 12 observation visits.

Recognitions include Guangdong Prefabricated Building Demonstration Project; Shenzhen 13th Five-Year Construction Technology Demonstration Project; 2019 Guangdong Outstanding Prefabricated Building Observation Project; Yuegang Award; Shenzhen Excellent Safety and Civilized Construction Site; Shenzhen Green Building Demonstration Site; Shenzhen Green Building Gold Design Certification; and second prize for Shenzhen Outstanding Construction QC Team Achievements.

An appraisal organized by the China Construction Metal Structure Association rated the overall system nationally leading and its lightweight wall-panel design and application internationally advanced. The system combines an all-steel main structure, steel-bar truss floor decking and prefabricated lightweight interior and exterior walls, providing an integrated solution with advantages in programme, energy efficiency, environmental performance and building functionality.

As GSIN's first prefabricated steel-building project, Cumark Tower has both earned recognition and provided experience for subsequent technological innovation.

/article/detail/234.html.title: GSIN receives its fourth Construction Steel Structure Industry Trustworthy Enterprise award
/article/detail/234.html.summary: The China Construction Metal Structure Association has named GSIN a 2021 Trustworthy Enterprise in the Construction Steel Structure Industry. This is the fourth time GSIN has received the honour since its first recognition in 2015.
/article/detail/234.html.bodyHtml:
The China Construction Metal Structure Association has named GSIN a 2021 Trustworthy Enterprise in the Construction Steel Structure Industry. This is the fourth time GSIN has received the honour since its first recognition in 2015.

The award supports national efforts to strengthen social credit systems, improve integrity in steel construction and promote a law-abiding, orderly market. Industry experts assess enterprise strength, operating scale, technical capability, innovation achievements, reputation, influence and market conduct.

The recognition acknowledges GSIN's capabilities and influence, as well as its commitment to lawful and trustworthy operations and steady development in a changing economy. GSIN will continue technical innovation, industrialization and product development in green construction, improving its innovation capacity and competitiveness.

/article/detail/232.html.title: 1,000-tonne steel skybridge successfully lifted at Kangtai Group Tower
/article/detail/232.html.summary: On 17 May, GSIN successfully completed overall lifting of the steel skybridge at Kangtai Group Tower.
/article/detail/232.html.bodyHtml:
On 17 May, GSIN successfully completed overall lifting of the steel skybridge at Kangtai Group Tower.

The project has a total floor area of approximately 139,500 m² and steel consumption of approximately 8,000 tonnes. Tower A is a 36-storey, 183.1 m composite R&D building; Tower B is a 19-storey, 76.45 m prefabricated dormitory. A two-storey steel truss skybridge connects the towers at the top of Tower B. Uses include basement parking, new industrial premises, dormitories and retail podiums. Structural systems include concrete-filled steel-tube frames with reinforced-concrete cores, frame–shear walls and steel trusses.

The skybridge connects floors 13–15 of Tower A and floors 16–19 of Tower B. Its lower chord is installed at 61.75 m and upper chord at 70.75 m. The completed bridge is approximately 17 m wide and 40 m long, with six main support trusses, each 9 m high. The projecting truss portion weighs approximately 1,000 tonnes.

Five hydraulic lifting units at five synchronized lifting points raised approximately 1,000 tonnes through 61.75 m in about nine hours. The team overcame the difficulties of the unusual skybridge through coordinated, precise and safe construction, adding another representative overall-lifting project to GSIN's experience.

/article/detail/233.html.title: GSIN departments hold Work Safety Month activities
/article/detail/233.html.summary: June marked the 21st national Work Safety Month, with the theme Observe the Work Safety Law and Fulfil the First Responsible Person's Duties. Following the national 2022 notice and taking epidemic-control conditions into account, GSIN organized activities to strengthen enterprise responsibility, safety awareness and staff protection.
/article/detail/233.html.bodyHtml:
June marked the 21st national Work Safety Month, with the theme Observe the Work Safety Law and Fulfil the First Responsible Person's Duties. Following the national 2022 notice and taking epidemic-control conditions into account, GSIN organized activities to strengthen enterprise responsibility, safety awareness and staff protection.

Safety education: Staff watched accident warning films and studied and were assessed on the Work Safety Law. Launch ceremonies and dedicated information boards supported the campaign. Factory and site workers took part in practical exercises including balance beams, helmet impacts, safety harnesses, falls through openings and electrical safety.

Hazard inspections: Second-quarter comprehensive inspections covered construction sites, dormitories and canteens. The I Am a Safety Whistleblower campaign encouraged staff to identify and correct risks, especially in accident-prone operations. Rewarded reporting of hazards and violations strengthened employee supervision. Department-led safety discussions examined gaps in responsibilities and their underlying causes.

Emergency drills: Production and fire-safety rescue exercises reinforced response procedures and escape skills. Emergency plans were reviewed to improve their rigour, relevance and practical operation.

Digital management: GSIN developed and refined an enterprise WeChat safety platform for dynamic assessment, training and visual data management. Production units were asked to use it to follow safety developments and improve efficiency.

The activities aimed to move staff from passive compliance to active, competent safety management, strengthen the safety foundation and sustain a stable working environment. GSIN will consolidate effective practices and continue them beyond the campaign month.

/article/detail/229.html.title: GSIN's complete building technology system enters Shenzhen's new construction technology catalogue
/article/detail/229.html.summary: On 18 January 2022, Shenzhen's Housing and Construction Bureau released its 2021 New Construction Technology Promotion Catalogue. GSIN's complete prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system was the only prefabricated steel-building technology among the 13 selected technologies.
/article/detail/229.html.bodyHtml:
On 18 January 2022, Shenzhen's Housing and Construction Bureau released its 2021 New Construction Technology Promotion Catalogue. GSIN's complete prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system was the only prefabricated steel-building technology among the 13 selected technologies.

The catalogue describes three integrated parts: an all-steel main structure, steel-bar truss floor decking and a lightweight exterior wall enclosure. The latter reduces dead load, improves wall connections and helps shorten construction programmes.

The system reflects nearly ten years of joint research with Tsinghua University and other universities and enterprises, applied to housing, schools, offices and hospitals. In 2018, a panel led by Academician Zhou Xuhong rated version 1.0 nationally advanced. In 2021, a panel led by Academician Yue Qingrui rated version 2.0 internationally advanced overall.

Applications include Ningxi Yuefu in Yancheng, featured in CCTV's Steel Backbone; Taizhou Nanyun Jiayuan, a 2021 Jiangsu demonstration project; Shenzhen Nanhua Primary School, part of the city's Double Ten programme; and Cumark Tower, a Guangdong prefabricated-building and Shenzhen construction-technology demonstration project.

Selection acknowledges GSIN's application of new technologies and processes. The company will continue innovation in green prefabricated steel construction.

/article/detail/230.html.title: GSIN holds its 2021 annual review and commendation meeting
/article/detail/230.html.summary: On 5 March, GSIN held its 2021 annual review and commendation meeting through a combination of in-person and video attendance. The main venue at headquarters linked with Yancheng, Dongtai, Fangchenggang and Hangzhou. Company leaders and middle managers from departments, business divisions and the factory attended.
/article/detail/230.html.bodyHtml:
On 5 March, GSIN held its 2021 annual review and commendation meeting through a combination of in-person and video attendance. The main venue at headquarters linked with Yancheng, Dongtai, Fangchenggang and Hangzhou. Company leaders and middle managers from departments, business divisions and the factory attended.

General Manager Zhang Jianshe delivered the report Steady Progress and Dynamic Development, reviewing 2021 and setting out 2022 priorities. These included implementing the overall strategy, focusing on development quality and economic results, adjusting responsibilities so project teams lead delivery and headquarters builds capability, strengthening standardized management and innovation, and maintaining the dual strategy of GSIN Steel Fabrication and GSIN Green Building.

Chairman Zhang Feng spoke on organizational change, cost reduction and efficiency. He recognized achievements in production, technology and marketing and examined current opportunities and challenges. With 2022 the second year of the 14th Five-Year Plan and the start of organizational reform, he set five requirements: comprehensive organizational change; improved processes and systems; internal market mechanisms; a value-creation-and-sharing distribution model; and specific cost-reduction and efficiency measures.

Leaders presented functional reports, operating responsibility agreements were signed with production departments, and outstanding teams and individuals from 2021 were recognized.

/article/detail/227.html.title: GSIN awarded Grade I qualification for steel-structure fabrication enterprises in China
/article/detail/227.html.summary: GSIN has received Grade I qualification for steel-structure fabrication enterprises in China.
/article/detail/227.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN has received Grade I qualification for steel-structure fabrication enterprises in China.

At the end of 2021, China Steel Construction Society Executive Vice President Liu Yi, Deputy Secretary-General Dai Changhe, Guangdong Steel Structure Association Secretary-General Wan Minfang and Society Industry Affairs Director Xie Na conducted an on-site assessment in Shenzhen.

The experts reviewed GSIN's completed projects, history and scale; financial assets; automated workshops; fabrication, testing, inspection and coating equipment; output and production value; research and technical management; technical complexity; enterprise management; and staffing. They recognized GSIN's contributions to steel-structure research, fabrication and construction.

The qualification arrived as 2022 began, supporting the company's combined GSIN Green Building and GSIN Steel Fabrication development strategy.

/article/detail/228.html.title: First high-altitude asymmetric steel skybridge successfully lifted at Futong Jiuyue Mansion
/article/detail/228.html.summary: In mid-January 2022, the high-level skybridge at Futong Jiuyue Mansion was successfully lifted into position. Located north of Xinsha Road in Futian District, Shenzhen, the project comprises three super high-rise towers and a kindergarten, with a total floor area of 185,533 m².
/article/detail/228.html.bodyHtml:
In mid-January 2022, the high-level skybridge at Futong Jiuyue Mansion was successfully lifted into position. Located north of Xinsha Road in Futian District, Shenzhen, the project comprises three super high-rise towers and a kindergarten, with a total floor area of 185,533 m².

The asymmetric, fully cantilevered skybridge links Towers 2 and 3 at elevation 95.4 m. It is 48.1 m long and 6.45 m wide and incorporates a swimming pool 16.6 m long and 5.6 m wide.

The mainly H-section steel trusses weigh approximately 190 tonnes; the acrylic pool panels approximately 40 tonnes; the lifted curtain-wall portion approximately 6 tonnes; and the lifting platform approximately 50 tonnes. GSIN used hydraulic overall lifting to position and connect the assembly, described in the release as more than 300 tonnes.

Drawing on experience in steel design and construction, the team developed a tray lifting approach for the cantilevered pool. It addressed extensive high-level welding, demanding weld quality, protection of acrylic panels and asymmetric loading. The trusses were accurately connected to the main structure. Fifteen days later, the steel tray was separated and safely returned to ground level.

/article/detail/224.html.title: Guangming Tian'an Cloud Park wins the 13th Guangdong Steel Structure Gold Award
/article/detail/224.html.summary: On 19 December 2021, GSIN attended the Guangdong Steel Structure Association's sixth third member congress and sixth fourth executive council meeting at Guangzhou Hongde International Hotel. GSIN's Guangming Tian'an Cloud Park project received the 13th Guangdong Steel Structure Gold Award (Yuegang Award), and project managers received Outstanding Technical Personnel recognition.
/article/detail/224.html.bodyHtml:
On 19 December 2021, GSIN attended the Guangdong Steel Structure Association's sixth third member congress and sixth fourth executive council meeting at Guangzhou Hongde International Hotel. GSIN's Guangming Tian'an Cloud Park project received the 13th Guangdong Steel Structure Gold Award (Yuegang Award), and project managers received Outstanding Technical Personnel recognition.

Located in Guangming District, Shenzhen, on the former Guangming Farm Phase II TFY23 development site, the international conference center has a total floor area of approximately 148,659.9 m², including 50,298.6 m² below ground, and uses 3,800 tonnes of steel.

In July 2021, experts reviewed quality, scale, difficulty, innovation and management under the Yuegang Award rules. They noted the use of several steel technologies promoted within the ministry's Ten New Technologies for Construction, improving technical standards, quality and safety.

The project involved numerous large components, long spans and widely distributed construction points. Drawing on 23 years of experience, the team managed overlapping steel and concrete work, crane travel and lifting on basement roof slabs, and installation of components up to 42.5 m long and 53 tonnes, as well as complex trusses of varying shapes. Project managers published three technical papers.

Tian'an Cloud Park forms part of Guangming Science City's education–research integration cluster and central area, supporting research, technology transfer and academic exchange. The award recognizes GSIN's contribution to this landmark conference facility and the district's development.

/article/detail/225.html.title: GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure building technology assessed as internationally advanced
/article/detail/225.html.summary: On 15 December 2021, an evaluation of Research and Engineering Application of Complete Technologies for GSIN Prefabricated Steel Buildings was held at Shenzhen Crowne Plaza Hotel. Li Qingwei, Secretary-General of the China Steel Construction Society, chaired the meeting.
/article/detail/225.html.bodyHtml:
On 15 December 2021, an evaluation of Research and Engineering Application of Complete Technologies for GSIN Prefabricated Steel Buildings was held at Shenzhen Crowne Plaza Hotel. Li Qingwei, Secretary-General of the China Steel Construction Society, chaired the meeting.

Academician Yue Qingrui led the panel, with national engineering survey and design masters Wang Lijun and Hou Zhaoxin as deputy leaders. Members included Professor Wang Zhan of South China University of Technology, Guangdong survey and design master Zhang Liangping, Professor Zhang Sumei of Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, and Chen Zhenming, Chief Engineer of China Construction Steel Structure Engineering.

The panel reviewed technical documents, research presentations and six international and domestic novelty-search reports. Following questions and discussion, it rated the overall achievement internationally advanced. The through-plate beam–column connection for prefabricated steel frames and the connection between new prefabricated reinforced-concrete floor slabs and steel beams were rated internationally leading.

The achievement represents ten years of collaboration with Tsinghua University and other research and industry partners. It follows the 2018 appraisal, led by Academician Zhou Xuhong, of GSIN's light-panel steel-building system as nationally advanced. GSIN and its partners will continue research and product development in prefabricated steel construction.

/article/detail/226.html.title: Taizhou Nanyun Jiayuan named a 2021 Jiangsu Prefabricated Building Demonstration Project
/article/detail/226.html.summary: On 30 December 2021, Jiangsu's housing authority released its building-industry modernization demonstration catalogue. Building 34 at Nanyun Jiayuan, delivered by GSIN, was selected as a 2021 Jiangsu Prefabricated Building Demonstration Project.
/article/detail/226.html.bodyHtml:
On 30 December 2021, Jiangsu's housing authority released its building-industry modernization demonstration catalogue. Building 34 at Nanyun Jiayuan, delivered by GSIN, was selected as a 2021 Jiangsu Prefabricated Building Demonstration Project.

The development in Gaogang District, Taizhou, has a floor area of approximately 160,000 m². Building 34 was jointly invested in and developed by Taizhou Hengjian Real Estate and Jinxi Boyuan Real Estate, and delivered by GSIN under EPC using its complete prefabricated steel-building technology.

Building 34 has a total floor area of 7,106 m², including 6,518.41 m² above ground, one basement level and 11 above-ground storeys. Storey height is 2.9 m and building height 36.90 m. It has a seismic fortification intensity of 7 degrees and a prefabrication rate of 84.2%.

Its all-steel braced frame combines H-section columns, unequal-flange H-section beams and composite steel-bar truss floor decking. Lower beam flanges are narrower than the walls to avoid exposed beams. Green ALC panels form single-layer interior walls and double-layer exterior walls. Dry, plaster-free construction saves water and materials; the envelope integrates insulation, acoustics, fire resistance and waterproofing.

BIM coordinates structural, building-services and interior design and shares information across design, fabrication and erection. Openings in beam webs allow services to pass through, with most services separated from the structure, increasing clear internal height and comfort.

Finished interiors use component-based partitions, factory prefabrication and on-site assembly, considering the whole building lifecycle. It is Taizhou's first prefabricated high-rise steel residential building and a 2021 provincial building-modernization demonstration project.

/article/detail/223.html.title: GSIN's low-carbon public-rental housing module showcased at the 9th Shenzhen International Low Carbon City Forum
/article/detail/223.html.summary: The 2021 Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Forum and 9th Shenzhen International Low Carbon City Forum took place on 16–17 December 2021. With the theme China's Carbon Path: Green Innovation and Global Action, it was guided by the National Development and Reform Commission and Guangdong government, hosted by Shenzhen government and organized by the city's development and reform commission, ecology and environment bureau and Longgang District government.
/article/detail/223.html.bodyHtml:
The 2021 Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Forum and 9th Shenzhen International Low Carbon City Forum took place on 16–17 December 2021. With the theme China's Carbon Path: Green Innovation and Global Action, it was guided by the National Development and Reform Commission and Guangdong government, hosted by Shenzhen government and organized by the city's development and reform commission, ecology and environment bureau and Longgang District government.

GSIN built and exhibited a low-carbon prefabricated steel public-rental housing module using its internationally advanced complete building technology. The unit, a little over 40 m², has a regular, open layout without intrusive columns or walls, accommodating varied lifestyles. Designed on a 600 mm module, it achieves a 90% prefabrication rate and is an AA-rated Low-Carbon Residential Building Demonstration Project.

The steel frame uses an innovative through-plate beam–column connection. Vertically arranged stiffeners increase concrete placement and venting space while retaining concealed beams and columns, supporting dense, well-placed concrete inside steel columns.

Double autoclaved lightweight concrete exterior wall panels are externally mounted to provide air and water tightness, insulation, acoustics and finish. Inset interior panels use dry construction, saving water and materials while improving installation efficiency and wall finish.

BIM-based services coordinate with the structure, envelope and interiors. Routing through beams and separating services avoids crossing conduits, improves usable space and simplifies maintenance. Interiors use low-carbon substrates and prefabricated installation. Roof-integrated photovoltaics can replace conventional materials or be mounted separately, supporting energy generation, insulation and waterproofing.

After nine years, the forum has become a platform for low-carbon development and quality growth. GSIN will continue research and knowledge sharing in response to ecological civilization and carbon-peaking and neutrality goals.

Special thanks: Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research; Xinhui Decoration Technology (Shenzhen); Guangzhou Eternit Building Systems; and Shenzhen Chuangyi New Energy Technology.

/article/detail/219.html.title: Steel structure tops out at Shanghai Reeb Brewery redevelopment
/article/detail/219.html.summary: On 18 November 2021, the final steel beam was installed at the Shanghai Reeb Brewery redevelopment, topping out a representative GSIN project in eastern China.
/article/detail/219.html.bodyHtml:
On 18 November 2021, the final steel beam was installed at the Shanghai Reeb Brewery redevelopment, topping out a representative GSIN project in eastern China.

Located at 379 Hongmei South Road, Minhang District, Shanghai, the project is planned with a 60% prefabrication rate and a two-star green-building design rating. China Construction Seventh Engineering Division is the general contractor.

Phase I comprises 20 buildings, 19 with prefabricated steel frames. Its floor area is 81,000 m², including 32,600 m² above ground and 48,400 m² below ground, using approximately 4,800 tonnes of steel.

Phases II and III total 144,934 m², including 104,394 m² above ground and 40,540 m² below ground, with approximately 17,000 tonnes of steel. Phase II includes Tower 21, with two basement levels, 22 above-ground storeys and a height of 99.9 m, and a podium with one basement level, six above-ground storeys and a height of 26.9 m.

Phase III comprises Tower 26 and Buildings 22–25 and 27. Tower 26 has two basement levels, 17 above-ground storeys and a height of 79.9 m. The other five buildings have one basement level, four or five above-ground storeys and heights of approximately 27.1 m.

Since the first column lift on 23 October 2019, GSIN's East China division coordinated more than 700 days of work. The owner, supervision team and general contractor recognized its delivery, safety and quality. Labour teams received Safe Team honours and strong results in behaviour-based safety assessments. China Construction Seventh Engineering Division named GSIN a Win-Win Cooperation Partner and Outstanding Cooperation Partner. Topping out establishes another regional application of GSIN's prefabricated steel-building technology.

/article/detail/220.html.title: Cumark Tower recognized as a Shenzhen Construction Science and Technology Demonstration Project
/article/detail/220.html.summary: Under Shenzhen's construction science and technology programme management rules (Shen Jian Gui [2020] No. 17) and the acceptance notice for key 13th Five-Year research projects, ten projects passed expert acceptance: four were designated Construction Technology Demonstration Projects and six were rated qualified. GSIN's Cumark Tower was among the four demonstration projects.
/article/detail/220.html.bodyHtml:
Under Shenzhen's construction science and technology programme management rules (Shen Jian Gui [2020] No. 17) and the acceptance notice for key 13th Five-Year research projects, ten projects passed expert acceptance: four were designated Construction Technology Demonstration Projects and six were rated qualified. GSIN's Cumark Tower was among the four demonstration projects.

The panel found that its complete prefabricated steel-structure light-panel system meets national and Shenzhen requirements for energy efficiency, emissions reduction, environmental protection and a circular economy. It reduces structural dead load and improves seismic performance while meeting envelope requirements, providing a useful demonstration for steel construction.

Innovations include externally mounted lightweight wall panels on a high-rise steel building and windows fixed to the structure through independent steel framing, with flexible connections to the lightweight exterior panels. The panel identified the complete system as suitable for wider promotion.

GSIN will strengthen research and the application of new technologies, processes, materials and products, working towards integrated prefabricated steel-building solutions and products.

/article/detail/212.html.title: GSIN receives three China Steel Structure Building awards
/article/detail/212.html.summary: At the China Construction Steel Structure Industry Conference in Wuhan on 28–29 May 2021, GSIN received three honours: the Shenwan Huiyun project won the 14th China Steel Structure Gold Award; Mao Chaojiang was named a National Outstanding Project Manager; and GSIN's complete prefabricated steel-structure light-panel technology received a 2021 second-prize science and technology award.
/article/detail/212.html.bodyHtml:
At the China Construction Steel Structure Industry Conference in Wuhan on 28–29 May 2021, GSIN received three honours: the Shenwan Huiyun project won the 14th China Steel Structure Gold Award; Mao Chaojiang was named a National Outstanding Project Manager; and GSIN's complete prefabricated steel-structure light-panel technology received a 2021 second-prize science and technology award.

Shenwan Huiyun Center is located in the Shenzhen Bay Super Headquarters Base. This release records a height of 358.7 m, four basement levels and 79 above-ground storeys. It describes the project as China's first deep excavation adjoining three metro lines and the tallest building above a metro development.

Mao Chaojiang graduated in civil engineering from Chongqing University, holds a first-class constructor qualification and has published four papers. His projects include Nanning China Resources MixC, Tencent Wuhan R&D Center and Shenwan Huiyun Center.

GSIN developed its light-panel steel-building system with the China Academy of Building Research, Tsinghua University and other partners, building on fabrication and erection experience. The company thanks the China Construction Metal Structure Association, experts and its project teams, and will continue improving industry technology and quality.

/article/detail/211.html.title: Carbon neutrality and steel structures: Building a greener future
/article/detail/211.html.summary: Carbon peaking and carbon neutrality entered China's government work report for the first time in 2021. Here carbon refers to carbon dioxide: peaking means total emissions reach a historic maximum and then decline; neutrality means human-caused emissions and removals balance over a defined period. At the 75th UN General Assembly in 2020, China announced its aim to peak emissions before 2030 and achieve neutrality before 2060.
/article/detail/211.html.bodyHtml:
Carbon peaking and carbon neutrality entered China's government work report for the first time in 2021. Here carbon refers to carbon dioxide: peaking means total emissions reach a historic maximum and then decline; neutrality means human-caused emissions and removals balance over a defined period. At the 75th UN General Assembly in 2020, China announced its aim to peak emissions before 2030 and achieve neutrality before 2060.

The China Building Energy Consumption Research Report 2020 states that whole-process building emissions reached 4.93 billion tonnes in 2018, or 51.3% of national emissions. Green buildings are important to meeting the sector's goals. The original article reports that prefabrication can save 90% of water and reduce waste, residues and air pollution by 70% compared with conventional construction.

Prefabricated steel buildings assemble factory-made components on site. Avoiding cast-in-place connections supports faster installation and more controllable quality. Steel's ductility supports seismic performance, its recyclability reduces environmental impact, and smaller beam and column sections can increase usable space. These features are extending its use from public buildings to housing.

GSIN has collaborated with the China Academy of Building Research, Tsinghua University, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research and Chongqing University on green-building systems for super high-rise, large-span and prefabricated structures.

Representative applications include Cumark Tower, a national two-star green building and Shenzhen green-construction demonstration and gold dual-label project; the Third High-Tech Prefabricated School under Shenzhen's Double Ten programme; Longgang District's infectious-disease treatment facility upgrade; temporary buildings at Zhengzhou Incubation Park; and EPC high-rise housing at Ningxi Yuefu in Dongtai and Nanyun Jiayuan in Taizhou.

After more than twenty years in green construction, GSIN continues to pursue safe, comfortable, healthy and durable living spaces and to contribute to carbon-neutral development.

/article/detail/210.html.title: GSIN prefabricated steel housing showcased at the 17th International Green Building and Building Energy Efficiency Conference
/article/detail/210.html.summary: GSIN exhibited a model of Dongtai Ningxi Yuefu and its prefabricated steel residential product system at the 17th International Green Building and Building Energy Efficiency Conference and New Technology and Product Expo, held in Chengdu on 18–19 May 2021.
/article/detail/210.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN exhibited a model of Dongtai Ningxi Yuefu and its prefabricated steel residential product system at the 17th International Green Building and Building Energy Efficiency Conference and New Technology and Product Expo, held in Chengdu on 18–19 May 2021.

The event supported the seven-ministry goal that green buildings account for 70% of new urban construction in 2022. It was organized by the Chinese Society for Urban Studies, Chengdu government, the US–China Green Fund, the Society's green-building and energy-efficiency committee and the International Future City Technology Innovation Alliance. Sessions covered research, trends, projects, standards, policy, assessment, design, optimized construction, ecological districts and carbon-peaking and neutrality pathways.

Ningxi Yuefu is in coastal central Jiangsu, facing the Yellow Sea and exposed to monsoons, humidity, high salinity and wind pressure. This release records 25 above-ground storeys, two basement levels, a height of 83.255 m and a floor area of 10,971 m². GSIN developed patented technologies for structural safety, wall insulation, window waterproofing, facade finish and interiors without exposed beams or columns.

Beams, columns, stairs and floors each achieve 100% component prefabrication. Large lightweight wall panels integrate insulation and finish, are made to design in the factory and installed dry on site. Under GB/T 51129-2017, the unfinished building already exceeds 60% prefabrication and qualifies as Grade A.

The above-ground steel structure and envelope took seven months, reported as 30% shorter than reinforced-concrete construction. The project saved 90% of scaffolding and 95% of formwork, while dry exterior-wall installation avoided replastering and saved approximately 190 m³ of water. Reduced temporary materials, storage needs, wet work, waste, dust and noise further supported greener construction.

GSIN will continue developing steel residential pilots and supporting construction-industry transformation and the wider adoption of green prefabricated buildings.

/article/detail/206.html.title: GSIN designated a National Prefabricated Building Industrial Base
/article/detail/206.html.summary: On 10 September 2020, the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development designated GSIN among the second batch of National Prefabricated Building Industrial Bases.
/article/detail/206.html.bodyHtml:
On 10 September 2020, the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development designated GSIN among the second batch of National Prefabricated Building Industrial Bases.

The ministry's notice (Jian Ban Biao Han [2020] No. 470), addressed to provincial housing authorities, the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps housing bureau and relevant organizations, implements national urban planning and prefabrication policies, including State Council Office Document [2016] No. 71. Following provincial recommendations and expert review, 18 cities including Chongqing, 12 industrial parks including Tianjin Modern Building Industrial Park, and 121 enterprises including Beijing Construction Engineering Group were selected.

The notice asks model cities and industrial bases to develop replicable practices and provide leadership and industrial support. Provincial authorities must supervise implementation; the ministry will conduct periodic assessments and withdraw recognition from bases that fail. The original notice includes lists of the selected cities and bases.

As construction modernizes, standardized fabrication and installation, low energy consumption and new materials are encouraging prefabrication. GSIN has worked with Kobe Steel, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research, Tsinghua University's civil engineering department, Chongqing University's architecture department and China Academy of Building Research on its light-panel steel-building system. At the time of this release, the system had accumulated 22 patent applications and three provincial construction methods.

Applications span business centers, high-rise housing, schools and hospitals, including Longgang Fourth People's Hospital, Nanyun Jiayuan and Nanhua Primary School. Completed in 2019, Cumark Tower received Shenzhen's first housing-authority recognition for a prefabricated steel building and the Yuegang Award. GSIN will use national-base recognition to continue researching and promoting prefabrication.

/article/detail/207.html.title: GSIN explores the next decade of prefabricated construction
/article/detail/207.html.summary: The third International Shenzhen Prefabricated Building Development Summit and Exhibition took place on 17–19 September at the InterContinental Shenzhen Dameisha Resort. More than 50 experts from across the supply chain discussed quality development in building industrialization. GSIN supported the event and participated in its enterprise exhibition.
/article/detail/207.html.bodyHtml:
The third International Shenzhen Prefabricated Building Development Summit and Exhibition took place on 17–19 September at the InterContinental Shenzhen Dameisha Resort. More than 50 experts from across the supply chain discussed quality development in building industrialization. GSIN supported the event and participated in its enterprise exhibition.

Organized by Shenzhen's building-industrialization association, the forum's theme was Leading the Era, Prefabricating the Next Decade. Guidance came from the ministry's science and industrialization center, Guangdong and Shenzhen housing authorities, the city's construction-industry Party committee and the prefabricated-building technology innovation alliance.

Chairman Zhang Feng spoke on Applying Integrated Thinking to Prefabricated Steel Buildings, introducing GSIN's approach through research, technology, independent assessments and projects.

The approach integrates the entire process and supply chain: policy and market research, project planning, multidisciplinary design, engineering support and user evaluation, alongside materials, factory fabrication, logistics, erection, optimization, operation and maintenance. Parallel coordination replaces sequential traditional workflows to integrate resources and shorten programmes.

In Shenzhen's 40th anniversary year, development of the Greater Bay Area and the demonstration zone creates new opportunities. GSIN will focus on customer needs, quality, efficiency and prefabrication research as the industry enters its next decade.

/article/detail/202.html.title: A home in 24 hours: Fully prefabricated steel-structure housing
/article/detail/202.html.summary: The Shenzhen International Finished Housing Exhibition concluded on 23 August. Its Challenge the Impossible project brought together Shenzhen Furniture Association's housing institute, Japanese housing designer Sadao Tsuchiya, GSIN, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research and industry partners to build a fully prefabricated, move-in-ready steel home on an empty site within 24 hours.
/article/detail/202.html.bodyHtml:
The Shenzhen International Finished Housing Exhibition concluded on 23 August. Its Challenge the Impossible project brought together Shenzhen Furniture Association's housing institute, Japanese housing designer Sadao Tsuchiya, GSIN, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research and industry partners to build a fully prefabricated, move-in-ready steel home on an empty site within 24 hours.

At 10:30 on 20 August, Shenzhen Deputy Secretary-General Li Zhuowen launched the challenge. At noon on 22 August, institute head Guan Yongkang announced success. Actual on-site construction took 18 hours and 15 minutes, almost six hours ahead of the target.

Preparation took nine months, 4.5 trial assemblies, two main-structure revisions and repeated connection improvements. Early trials exposed the lack of integration among the building, interiors and component systems. The lesson was to develop a complete building system rather than treat prefabrication as only an efficient construction method.

From the two-storey exhibition home to 25-storey residential and public buildings, integration should follow consistent modular design, component modules, standardized spaces and assembly-based construction. Standard unit types can be combined into four-bay modules, individual blocks and multiple blocks, while steel's long spans and column-free interiors enable adaptable layouts, even on constrained sites.

GSIN's booth showcased the residential system jointly developed with Tsuchiya, the general institute's design studio and the housing institute. Designed by Tsuchiya, it expressed steel and lightweight walls through physical connections, models and technical displays. Chairman Zhang Feng presented the system's introduction and applications at the industry forum.

The event strengthened international awareness and supply-chain coordination from structure to interiors. GSIN thanks Sadao Tsuchiya, Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research, Shenzhen Furniture Association's housing institute and all challenge partners. The original article also presents Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center, which GSIN helped build.

/article/detail/201.html.title: Forty years of Shenzhen: Witnessing change through steel structures
/article/detail/201.html.summary: On the 40th anniversary of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, GSIN celebrates the city's transformation from a fishing village into a metropolis. Founded in 1998 with ten people and grown to a national high-tech enterprise of more than 300, GSIN has spent 22 years participating in that development.

On the 40th anniversary of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, GSIN celebrates the city's transformation from a fishing village into a metropolis. Founded in 1998 with ten people and grown to a national high-tech enterprise of more than 300, GSIN has spent 22 years participating in that development.

Representative super high-rise projects include Shenwan Huiyun Center, Shenzhen Bay One, Bojin Business Plaza, Shenzhen Stock Exchange Operations Center, ICBC Shenzhen Tower, Guoyin Minsheng Financial Center, the Shenzhen branch towers of China Merchants Bank and China Construction Bank, China Mobile Information Tower, Wongtee Tower, Zhengqi Future City, Southern University of Science and Technology, Excellence Meilin Center, Jinlitong Tower, Richinfo Technology Tower and Das Intellitech Tower.

Large-span projects include Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center, Shenzhen MSU–BIT University, Shenzhen Sports Center's swimming hall, Shenzhen Airport Ground Transportation Center, Universiade Center, UPS Asia-Pacific air hub, Bao'an Sports Center natatorium, Kaisa Golden Bay International Park, Metro Line 9 maintenance depot, Shekou Sea World, Chunhua Footbridge and 11 pedestrian bridges on Shennan Road.

Prefabricated steel projects include Cumark Tower, Third High-Tech Prefabricated School (Nanhua Primary School), Longgang Fourth People's Hospital and Guangming Science City Exhibition Center.

Historical figures in this release include Huiyun Center: 79 storeys, 358.7 m; Shenzhen Bay One: 76 storeys, 341.4 m; Bojin Towers A and B: 268.4 m and 200.3 m; Shenzhen Stock Exchange: 48 storeys, 245.8 m; the exhibition center: 620,000 m² and 270,000 tonnes of steel; MSU–BIT University: 126,800 m² and a 156.4 m spire; Chunhua Footbridge: a 217.5 m ring; Cumark Tower: 76.4 m and 38,697 m²; and Nanhua Primary School: 48 classes, 2,160 places, completed in four months.

The article also highlights bridges on Caitian, Shangbu, Binhe and Xinzhou roads and GSIN's recognition as an Outstanding Organization for Shenzhen Special Economic Zone's 40th anniversary.

/article/detail/199.html.title: A new landmark: Steel structure topped out at the 358.7 m Shenwan Huiyun Center
/article/detail/199.html.summary: At 9:30 on 26 July, representatives of Shenzhen Metro, Vanke, China Construction First Group, Shenzhen AUBE Engineering Design Consultants, Shenzhen Huaxi Construction Management and GSIN gathered to mark topping out of Shenwan Huiyun Center's main steel structure.
/article/detail/199.html.bodyHtml:
At 9:30 on 26 July, representatives of Shenzhen Metro, Vanke, China Construction First Group, Shenzhen AUBE Engineering Design Consultants, Shenzhen Huaxi Construction Management and GSIN gathered to mark topping out of Shenwan Huiyun Center's main steel structure.

As an early project in the Shenzhen Bay Super Headquarters Base, the tower is recorded here as 358.7 m high, with four basement levels, 79 above-ground storeys and approximately 35,000 tonnes of steel. It uses a mega-frame, core tube and outrigger-truss system and is described as China's tallest building above a metro development.

Mega steel-reinforced perimeter columns reach 2.4 × 2.85 m in section; the heaviest column lift is 33.2 tonnes. Giant cruciform outrigger nodes measure up to 5.5 × 5.5 × 3 m, with a maximum truss lift of 40.6 tonnes. Below floor 12, a truss-suspended floor system opens up the main lobby.

From the first mega-column lift in 2017 to the last beam in 2020, the team overcame a demanding programme, complex construction and high technical requirements. GSIN continued to apply its values of integrity, diligence, gratitude and innovation, aiming for the China Construction Steel Structure Gold Award.

Milestones shown in the article: high-rise construction accelerated in February 2018; the tower passed 200 m in January 2019 and 300 m in October 2019; the main steel structure topped out on 26 July 2020. GSIN pays tribute to everyone involved in building this waterfront landmark.

/article/detail/200.html.title: Maintaining strategic focus, overcoming challenges and advancing GSIN's development
/article/detail/200.html.summary: On 15 August 2020, GSIN held its first-half review in the company lecture hall to assess performance, plan the second half and examine management issues. Departments, business divisions and senior leaders presented reports. Chairman Zhang Feng spoke on maintaining strategic focus, confronting difficulties, transforming and upgrading for quality development.
/article/detail/200.html.bodyHtml:
On 15 August 2020, GSIN held its first-half review in the company lecture hall to assess performance, plan the second half and examine management issues. Departments, business divisions and senior leaders presented reports. Chairman Zhang Feng spoke on maintaining strategic focus, confronting difficulties, transforming and upgrading for quality development.

The meeting emphasized that steel construction's cost advantages depend first on scale, then management and the ability to change. Competitive prefabricated steel construction requires technical, market and management advantages.

Safety performance was stable in the first half. The second half would retain safety as a prerequisite for production, select quality projects and prioritize cash flow. Strengths included teams, strategic customers, regional reputation, fabrication bases, Grade I specialist qualification, an established prefabricated system and industrial-base recognition. Constraints remained in costs, capital, management, brand and capacity.

Priorities were to consolidate strategic customers, reduce costs, improve results and actively develop prefabricated steel business. GSIN would retain its dual GSIN Steel Fabrication and GSIN Green Building strategy, steadily advancing transformation towards prefabrication while refining traditional steel work. Leaders were asked to act on that strategy, adapt to change and avoid complacency.

/article/detail/198.html.title: How was a prefabricated steel school with 2,160 places built in four months?
/article/detail/198.html.summary: The Third High-Tech Prefabricated School is northeast of the intersection of Shennan Avenue and Huanggang Road in Futian District, Shenzhen. It occupies approximately 12,000 m², with a floor area of 12,319 m², 48 classes and 2,160 school places. It was among the first projects under Futian's Double Ten programme of ten permanent and ten prefabricated schools.
/article/detail/198.html.bodyHtml:
The Third High-Tech Prefabricated School is northeast of the intersection of Shennan Avenue and Huanggang Road in Futian District, Shenzhen. It occupies approximately 12,000 m², with a floor area of 12,319 m², 48 classes and 2,160 school places. It was among the first projects under Futian's Double Ten programme of ten permanent and ten prefabricated schools.

The school uses a full steel frame, steel-bar truss decking and ALC interior and exterior walls. It achieved a 76% prefabrication rate, structural topping out in 30 days and full handover in four months. The original presentation sets out five core concepts and six technical advantages.

Conventional construction faces energy use, pollution, low productivity and labour constraints. Standardized design, factory fabrication, assembly-based construction, digital management and intelligent operation provide a path towards greener, more sustainable building methods.

Special thanks: China Construction Seventh Engineering Division; China Academy of Building Research; Shenzhen Futian District Education Bureau; and Shenzhen Jiuzhou Construction Technology. Source: GSIN Green Building Division.

/article/detail/191.html.title: GSIN's first EPC prefabricated steel housing project, Nanyun Jiayuan, breaks ground
/article/detail/191.html.summary: On the morning of 14 January 2020, representatives of the developer, designers and supervision team attended the groundbreaking of Nanyun Jiayuan's prefabricated steel housing in Gaogang District, Taizhou.
/article/detail/191.html.bodyHtml:
On the morning of 14 January 2020, representatives of the developer, designers and supervision team attended the groundbreaking of Nanyun Jiayuan's prefabricated steel housing in Gaogang District, Taizhou.

The approximately 160,000 m² development is Taizhou's first prefabricated steel-building project and is planned as a premium modern Chinese-style community. This release records Building 34 as 36.4 m high, with 11 above-ground storeys, one basement level and a total floor area of 7,300 m². Each floor has four apartments of approximately 140–150 m².

The project uses GSIN's light-panel steel-building system: H-section beams and columns, steel-bar truss floor decking, double exterior ALC panels of 150 + 75 mm and interior ALC panels with finish boards. Prefabrication exceeds 80%.

As GSIN's first EPC prefabricated high-rise steel residential project, Nanyun Jiayuan will be delivered through coordinated planning, careful organization and strict quality controls.

/article/detail/192.html.title: Long-cantilever hotel roof trusses successfully lifted at Shenzhen Jinshawan
/article/detail/192.html.summary: On 10 January 2020, the final main truss of the Jinshawan International Hotel's 32 m cantilevered roof was installed, witnessed by teams from China Construction First Group, GSIN and Shenzhen Keyu Engineering Consultants.
/article/detail/192.html.bodyHtml:
On 10 January 2020, the final main truss of the Jinshawan International Hotel's 32 m cantilevered roof was installed, witnessed by teams from China Construction First Group, GSIN and Shenzhen Keyu Engineering Consultants.

The Jinshawan International Park project is on the waterfront in Dapeng New District, Shenzhen. Its performing arts center evokes layered feathers of a roc, while the hotel roof represents golden wings. The project uses 2,320 tonnes of steel; the performing arts roof and hotel cantilever were key construction challenges.

The hotel's tubular-truss roof has an approximately 20 m supported section and a 32 m cantilever, 15 support points and a width of 18.25 m. Five main and 16 secondary trusses are stabilized by horizontal ties at upper- and lower-chord levels. The cantilever stands 27.3 m above ground, making lifting, welding and coating demanding high-level operations. Dry winter conditions also required careful fire control, and intersecting tubular welds demanded precise installation.

Temporary supports were placed on the east tower's concrete structure beneath the five main cantilever trusses. A 225-tonne crawler crane in tower configuration combined sectional lifts with individual assembly. After weld testing, synchronized staged release unloaded the structure, followed by high-level corrosion and fire protection coating from articulated platforms. The specialist safety plan passed expert review on 30 December 2019.

The performing arts roof comprises six leaves and combines intersecting, cast-steel, welded-ball, pin, welded and bolted joints with multi-slope tubular trusses, unusual tree-shaped tubes, single-layer solid-web grids and portal frames. In-situ sectional lifting and individual assembly were selected to suit tower cranes and site conditions. Repeated construction simulations optimized unloading and support-removal sequences.

Numerous cast-steel nodes with varied pipe directions required a dedicated acceptance plan. Connections to ordinary steel also required a dissimilar-metal welding procedure qualification, witnessed by relevant personnel, providing experience for similar projects.

/article/detail/194.html.title: GSIN's top ten milestones of 2019
/article/detail/194.html.summary: 2019 began GSIN's fifth five-year plan and brought important progress in transformation. The year's ten milestones, as recorded in this retrospective, were:
/article/detail/194.html.bodyHtml:
2019 began GSIN's fifth five-year plan and brought important progress in transformation. The year's ten milestones, as recorded in this retrospective, were:

1. Industrial-base and demonstration recognition: GSIN joined the first batches of Guangdong and Shenzhen Prefabricated Building Industrial Bases. Cumark Tower's EPC project joined Guangdong's first demonstration projects and received the 2019 Outstanding Observation Project honour.

2. Industry integrity: In May 2019, GSIN was recognized as a 2018 Trustworthy Enterprise in China's Steel Structure Industry, repeating its 2016 recognition.

3. Quality awards: Tencent Wuhan R&D Center received the 2018–2019 National Quality Engineering Award in December, following Huizhou Central Stadium's 2011 award. Shenzhen CCB Tower and Bojin Business Plaza received the 13th China Steel Structure Gold Award in May. GSIN had then won eight such gold awards across high-rise, urban-complex, industrial and sports projects.

4. Guangming Science City: In July, the 4,390 m² exhibition center on a 15,200 m² site was completed in 35 days despite heat, rain and typhoons, with around-the-clock work.

5. Green-building standards: Shenzhen's Green Building Construction Quality Acceptance Standard, to which GSIN contributed, was published in March 2019, strengthening whole-process supervision and technical support for acceptance.

6. Technology and industry exchange: GSIN hosted the August mid-year industrial-base meeting, attended by 56 representatives from 28 organizations and relevant authorities. Cumark Tower's light-panel system was selected for Shenzhen's key 13th Five-Year construction technology research programme in November.

7. Shanghai Reeb Brewery: GSIN signed a RMB 280 million construction contract for the redevelopment at 379 Hongmei South Road, Minhang District. The approximately 71,900 m² site and 287,300 m² total floor area were planned for offices, retail and modern housing.

8. Nanyun Jiayuan: Groundbreaking took place in January 2020 in Gaogang District, Taizhou. The company's first EPC prefabricated high-rise steel residential project is recorded here as 36.4 m high, with 11 above-ground storeys, one basement level and approximately 7,300 m².

9. Shenzhen anniversary honours: In January 2020, Shenzhen's civil engineering and architectural society named GSIN an Outstanding Construction Organization for the Special Economic Zone's 40th anniversary and Chairman Zhang Feng an Outstanding Individual.

10. Labour honour: General Office Director Kang Baorong received the 2019 Guangdong May 1 Labour Medal in April.

Looking to 2020, GSIN would retain its dual Green Building and Steel Fabrication strategy, improve development quality and pursue its responsibility to build homes people can trust.

/article/detail/195.html.title: GSIN holds its 2019 annual review: Reaching higher and making further breakthroughs

Departments reported their work and Chairman Zhang Feng delivered New Starting Point, New Track, New Requirements and New Breakthroughs: Improving Competitiveness from the Supply Side.
/article/detail/195.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN held its 2019 annual review and 2020 planning meeting on 5 March 2020, combining an on-site venue with online broadcasting because of the epidemic. Departments reported their work and Chairman Zhang Feng delivered New Starting Point, New Track, New Requirements and New Breakthroughs: Improving Competitiveness from the Supply Side.

Despite economic pressure and stricter safety and environmental requirements, departments expanded markets, supported key projects, managed risks and improved lean management and innovation. Contract value reached a new level of RMB 500 million.

For 2020, the final year of the 13th Five-Year Plan and a key year in GSIN's fifth five-year plan, the company would retain the Steel Fabrication and Green Building strategy while increasing green-building activity. More research and staffing would refine a reliable, functional, reasonably priced, healthy light-panel steel-building system.

To develop the Greater Bay Area market, Guangzhou and Shenzhen divisions were combined into a South China division focused on the Pearl River Delta. Xiamen became an East China division focused on the Yangtze River Delta. The Green Building division would transition towards general contracting. Two wholly owned subsidiaries, GSIN Steel Fabrication and GSIN General Contracting, would support a platform-based group.

The new prefabricated-building track would demand stronger capabilities and further growth from the RMB 500 million base. GSIN would focus on high-quality, cost-effective products and work towards becoming a national industry benchmark.

/article/detail/190.html.title: Tencent Wuhan R&D Center receives the National Quality Engineering Award
/article/detail/190.html.summary: At the 2019 National Quality Engineering Awards conference, held on 8 December at Beijing's China National Convention Center, Tencent Wuhan R&D Center received the 2018–2019 National Quality Engineering Award. It followed GSIN's award for Huizhou Central Stadium in 2011.
/article/detail/190.html.bodyHtml:
At the 2019 National Quality Engineering Awards conference, held on 8 December at Beijing's China National Convention Center, Tencent Wuhan R&D Center received the 2018–2019 National Quality Engineering Award. It followed GSIN's award for Huizhou Central Stadium in 2011.

Located beside Tangxun Lake in Jiangxia, Wuhan, Hubei, the reclining-penguin-shaped building has approximately 73,000 m² of floor area, five above-ground storeys and two basement levels, a height of about 30 m and a folded roof. This historical article records 4,170 tonnes of steel, completion in August 2015 and the 2015 China Construction Steel Structure Gold Award.

The structure combines a steel-reinforced concrete frame with roof trusses, suspended floors and local cantilevered steelwork. Hanger columns transfer suspended-floor loads through the roof trusses to the main structure.

The roof has 12 planar single-layer trusses: eight primary and four secondary, using box and welded H sections. The lower chord is at 22.2 m and the upper chord follows the roof profile. The maximum main-truss cantilever is 20 m; secondary spans reach 42.5 m; the heaviest individual truss is 42 tonnes. Floors three to five hang from the main roof trusses.

/article/detail/187.html.title: Shenzhen housing authority's prefabricated-building trainees visit GSIN's Guangdong industrial base

To strengthen local prefabrication skills, Shenzhen's Housing and Construction Bureau and building-industrialization association organized the 2019 Whole-Process Prefabricated Building Technology and Case Training series.

Participants represented authorities, developers, contractors, designers, component manufacturers, supervisors and consultants. They exchanged experience and showed strong interest in prefabricated steel buildings.

Building on fabrication and erection expertise, GSIN will continue developing steel housing and its light-panel system. /article/detail/189.html.title: GSIN's light-panel steel building system selected for Shenzhen's 13th Five-Year construction research programme
/article/detail/189.html.summary: At the 21st China Hi-Tech Fair, Shenzhen's Housing and Construction Bureau released the city's key 13th Five-Year construction science and technology programme. Cumark Tower, built with GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure light-panel system, was selected.
/article/detail/189.html.bodyHtml:
At the 21st China Hi-Tech Fair, Shenzhen's Housing and Construction Bureau released the city's key 13th Five-Year construction science and technology programme. Cumark Tower, built with GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure light-panel system, was selected.

The programme comprises 144 projects: four soft-science projects, 68 R&D projects, 37 technology-application projects, 33 construction standards and two international or cross-border cooperation projects. It covers survey, design, construction, new technology, green building, industrialization and intelligent construction.

Cumark Tower combines a steel main structure, steel-bar truss floor decking and ALC walls, using standardized design, factory fabrication, assembly and digital management. The source describes it as South China's first prefabricated high-rise steel building; in 2019 it joined Guangdong's first demonstration projects. Its prefabrication design assessment scored 90 points, and a national panel led by Academician Zhou Xuhong appraised the technology.

GSIN will use Greater Bay Area and demonstration-zone opportunities to advance its Green Building and Steel Fabrication strategy, integrating R&D, design, construction and operations, improving its system and strengthening its brand.

On 19 July 2019, GSIN was approved as one of Shenzhen's first prefabricated-building industrial bases, following its recognition in Guangdong's first group. The report records 22 patent applications and three provincial construction methods. Cumark Tower's distinctions included Guangdong prefabricated-building demonstration recognition, the 2017 Yuegang Award, provincial and Shenzhen safety and civilized-construction awards, Shenzhen Excellent Structural Engineering, green-building design recognition, China Construction Seventh Engineering Division's CI Gold Award, Shenzhen safety demonstration recognition, a second-prize QC award and green-construction demonstration recognition.

Applications included Cumark Tower, Nanyun Jiayuan and the Longgang hospital project.
