/article/detail/177.html.title: Guangming Science City Exhibition Center: A record of 35 days of construction
/article/detail/177.html.summary: This account pays tribute to the team that delivered the Guangming Science City Exhibition Center in 35 days. The general-contracting project covered a floor area of 4,390 m² on a 15,200 m² site, with 92 machines, 396 workers and numerous specialist subcontractors working across disciplines.
/article/detail/177.html.bodyHtml:
This account pays tribute to the team that delivered the Guangming Science City Exhibition Center in 35 days. The general-contracting project covered a floor area of 4,390 m² on a 15,200 m² site, with 92 machines, 396 workers and numerous specialist subcontractors working across disciplines.

Work sometimes began at 4 a.m. and continued around the clock through heat, rain and typhoon conditions. Staff ate and slept on site, coordinated until their voices became hoarse and continued to support their colleagues despite exhaustion and illness.

The account describes muddy clothing, sweat-soaked shifts and time away from family, including missed parent meetings and children's final-exam preparation. Although home could be only a 90-minute journey away, some team members did not return for more than 30 days.

It credits ordinary workers' responsibility, persistence and coordination with keeping the company's delivery promise and earning the client's trust and respect.

/article/detail/172.html.title: Expert appraisal of GSIN's prefabricated steel light-panel building system held at Cumark Tower
/article/detail/172.html.summary: On 15 June 2018, the China Construction Metal Structure Association organized an expert appraisal of GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system at Cumark Tower.
/article/detail/172.html.bodyHtml:
On 15 June 2018, the China Construction Metal Structure Association organized an expert appraisal of GSIN's prefabricated steel-structure light-panel building system at Cumark Tower.

Participants included Academician Zhou Xuhong of Chongqing University, Wang Lijun, Tsinghua University's Wang Yuanqing, a deputy president of the China Institute of Building Standard Design and Research, Tongji University's Zhang Qilin, Chen Zhenming of China Construction Steel Structure, Liu Jian of the China Academy of Building Research's Shenzhen branch and association representative Hu Yuke.

The panel reviewed design, R&D and engineering applications, technical reports and test results, visited the project and questioned the development team. It recognized the system's functional completeness, compliance with national assessment requirements, high prefabrication rate, shorter construction programme and orderly site.

The appraisal discussed savings in materials, water, energy, land and labour, together with environmental benefits. Recommendations included further optimization against established systems, integrated interiors and a broader range of panel types and specifications for different steel residential buildings. Chairman Zhang Feng thanked the panel and committed to implementing its recommendations.

/article/detail/173.html.title: GSIN holds its first-half 2018 review meeting
/article/detail/173.html.summary: GSIN held its 2018 first-half work review on 31 August and 1 September. Chairman and General Manager Zhang Feng called for strategy-led work, a more practical working style and completion of annual tasks. Business and departmental leaders reported on their work.
/article/detail/173.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN held its 2018 first-half work review on 31 August and 1 September. Chairman and General Manager Zhang Feng called for strategy-led work, a more practical working style and completion of annual tasks. Business and departmental leaders reported on their work.

Five priorities were set: solve problems through continuous improvement; strengthen basic management and system execution; involve all staff in marketing led by executives, departments and production teams; put safety first; and improve the light-panel building system as a flagship product.

The meeting reaffirmed the combined steel-structure and green-building strategy and the transition from fabrication and installation to complete prefabricated-building EPC contracting. Organization, processes and people would support market development, R&D, performance management and brand building.

/article/detail/174.html.title: Guangming District prefabricated-building training held at Cumark Tower

/article/detail/175.html.title: GSIN holds its 2018 annual review meeting
/article/detail/175.html.summary: On 23–24 February, GSIN reviewed 2018 performance and planned work for 2019. Chairman Zhang Feng called for stronger management and technical capabilities.
/article/detail/175.html.bodyHtml:
On 23–24 February, GSIN reviewed 2018 performance and planned work for 2019. Chairman Zhang Feng called for stronger management and technical capabilities.

The five-year strategy combines steel structures and green buildings, closes the design gap in EPC delivery, increases R&D investment and moves the company from labour-intensive fabrication and installation towards technology- and management-led development.

The 2018 review included the 357 m Shenwan Huiyun Center and four standard exhibition halls with 99 m spans at the major convention and exhibition complex. Green-building applications included Cumark Tower, described in the report as South China's first complete high-rise prefabricated steel building; the Longgang hospital temporary-relocation project; and the Red'ao Village refectory.

GSIN signed an agreement with Jinxi Real Estate and negotiated the Nanyun Jiayuan contract, its first EPC fully finished commercial residential project using steel and ALC panels. Experience covered public offices, sports buildings, hospitals and housing, including design, construction, management and after-sales service.

For 2019, the company would maintain its strategy, expand green-building EPC delivery and improve quality and efficiency. Priorities were management, especially safety; technical leadership; marketing breakthroughs; conversion of early-mover advantages into market benefits; and team development. After 21 years, GSIN aimed to become an industry benchmark.

/article/detail/163.html.title: A new chapter: GSIN holds its NEEQ listing bell ceremony in Beijing
/article/detail/163.html.summary: On 27 December 2016, Shenzhen GSIN Green Building Co., Ltd. held its listing bell ceremony at the National Equities Exchange and Quotations center on Financial Street, Xicheng District, Beijing. /article/detail/163.html.bodyHtml:
On 27 December 2016, Shenzhen GSIN Green Building Co., Ltd. held its listing bell ceremony at the National Equities Exchange and Quotations center on Financial Street, Xicheng District, Beijing. Chairman Zhang Feng and company leaders attended. Trading under stock code 839696, the company had formally listed on 16 November.

Zhang said the company would use the platform to support transformation, innovation and management improvement, guided by honesty, commitment, diligence and shared success. He thanked partners and employees who had helped the business grow from a small workshop in 1998 to a listed company employing hundreds of people.

In an interview with CCTV's securities-information channel, Zhang explained that listing would support standardized operations, employee belonging and access to capital. GSIN would build on its super-high-rise and long-span expertise while developing integrated prefabricated steel buildings.

The company outlined its transition from specialist steel contracting to green-building general contracting, primarily through EPC, to provide safer, greener and more livable buildings.

/article/detail/164.html.title: GSIN's March activities

/article/detail/165.html.title: GSIN holds its first-half 2017 review meeting

On 5 August 2017, GSIN held its first-half work review, chaired by Deputy General Manager Shen Bing. Chairman Zhang Feng, Deputy General Manager Zhang Jianshe, Chief Engineer Wang Jianhe and departmental leaders attended.

/article/detail/167.html.title: Cumark Tower tops out: Shenzhen's first prefabricated high-rise building

/article/detail/167.html.bodyHtml:
Cumark Tower's main steel structure topped out on 26 October 2017. Delivered by GSIN under an EPC model, the project was presented as Shenzhen's first fully prefabricated steel building and first three-star green high-rise prefabricated steel project. Partners included China Construction Seventh Engineering Division, Germany's Ytong and Japan's Kikusui Chemical.

Guests included Hao Yingji of the Shenzhen Energy Conservation Association, Cumark Chairman Li Ruichang, GSIN Chairman Zhang Feng, Si Xiang of China Construction Seventh Engineering Division's Southern Company, Hu Zhiyi of Shenzhen Hechuang Construction Engineering Consultants, Liu Jian of the China Academy of Building Research's Shenzhen branch and Ying Bo of China Construction First Engineering Division.

Speakers praised quality, technology and safety. Zhang thanked the client, design and construction partners and the project team led by Wang Jin. He described GSIN's transition from Grade I specialist contracting to EPC green-building delivery, integrating steel structures, ALC envelopes, finished interiors and intelligent systems.

Located in Guangming's technology industrial park, the project occupies 7,654 m², with approximately 38,697 m² of floor area, two basement levels and 17 above-ground storeys, rising 69.9 m. The system was developed with the China Academy of Building Research, Tsinghua University and Chongqing University. Prefabrication and assembly rates both exceeded 80%.

The report describes advantages in seismic performance, cost, programme and environmental impact, with whole-life savings in energy, land, water and materials and healthier, more comfortable and efficient spaces.

/article/detail/169.html.bodyHtml:
On 2 November, nearly 100 representatives from developers, supervisors and contractors attended a Guangming construction quality and safety exchange at Cumark Tower, which had received Shenzhen's Excellent Safe and Civilized Construction Site award. Subdistrict offices, the public-works bureau and water-management organizations supported the event.

The quality and safety supervision station called on project teams to prevent hazards and defects early and use the exchange to strengthen shared understanding and confidence.

Chairman Zhang Feng introduced the project, GSIN's EPC transition and its light-panel system. Cumark Tower's prefabrication and assembly rates both exceeded 80%; the report describes it as Shenzhen's first prefabricated steel building and first three-star green high-rise of its kind.

Ba Wensheng of China Construction Seventh Engineering Division's Shenzhen business unit explained safety and quality management: clear systems, standardized processes, early planning, ongoing supervision and improvement activities to resolve technical issues.

Guangming's housing and planning authority encouraged participants to apply the lessons. An organized site tour concluded the event, emphasizing quality, green construction, safety and civilized site management.

/article/detail/170.html.title: GSIN's 2017 annual review meeting concludes successfully
/article/detail/170.html.summary: GSIN held its 2017 annual review on 9–10 March, assessing achievements, current challenges and priorities for 2018. Chairman and General Manager Zhang Feng outlined a combined steel-structure and green-building strategy, stronger EPC capabilities and a transition to new growth drivers.
/article/detail/170.html.bodyHtml:
GSIN held its 2017 annual review on 9–10 March, assessing achievements, current challenges and priorities for 2018. Chairman and General Manager Zhang Feng outlined a combined steel-structure and green-building strategy, stronger EPC capabilities and a transition to new growth drivers.

Five priorities were set: strengthen both business lines and their divisions; invest in R&D and technical innovation; pursue multi-level, multi-channel proactive marketing; improve basic management to support the divisions; and use culture, policy and mutual support to enable shared development.

The five-year strategy would close the EPC design gap and move from labour-intensive fabrication and installation towards technology-led research and management, improving development quality.

Business divisions and departments reported on their work. Participants signed business and safety responsibility agreements and exchanged experience. The meeting emphasized disciplined safety, quality, management and cost control.

On 26 April 2018, the Shenzhen Green Building Association visited Cumark Tower for a member exchange on connecting the green-building industrial chain. The association organized member participation and GSIN hosted the site visit.

Secretary-General Wang Xiangyu chaired the meeting and introduced the participants. Chairman Zhang Feng presented the project. Chief Engineer Wang Jianhe, project technical lead Wang Lanrong and Luda Technology project manager Pei Pei discussed the prefabricated steel-structure light-panel system, site construction and advantages in green-building assessment.

Participants then toured the building and exchanged views on technical applications and cooperation.
